from leaderboard.standings import Player, rank


def test_tied_players_ordered_alphabetically():
    """When players have equal points, they should be ordered alphabetically.
    
    This test reproduces the bug where the same two players tied on points
    appear in different orders depending on other players in the list.
    """
    # Scenario 1: Reporter and Dave tied, with Adam below them
    players_scenario1 = [
        Player("Adam", 50),
        Player("Dave", 100),
        Player("Reporter", 100),
    ]
    ranked1 = rank(players_scenario1)
    # When tied at 100 points, Dave and Reporter should be alphabetically ordered
    # Dave comes before Reporter alphabetically
    assert ranked1[0].name == "Dave"
    assert ranked1[1].name == "Reporter"
    assert ranked1[2].name == "Adam"
    
    # Scenario 2: Reporter and Adam tied, with Dave above them
    players_scenario2 = [
        Player("Adam", 100),
        Player("Dave", 150),
        Player("Reporter", 100),
    ]
    ranked2 = rank(players_scenario2)
    # When tied at 100 points, Adam and Reporter should be alphabetically ordered
    # Adam comes before Reporter alphabetically
    assert ranked2[0].name == "Dave"
    assert ranked2[1].name == "Adam"
    assert ranked2[2].name == "Reporter"
    
    # Scenario 3: Same players as scenario 1, verify consistency
    # The relative order of Dave and Reporter should be the same
    ranked3 = rank(players_scenario1)
    dave_pos_1 = next(i for i, p in enumerate(ranked3) if p.name == "Dave")
    reporter_pos_1 = next(i for i, p in enumerate(ranked3) if p.name == "Reporter")
    
    # Dave should always come before Reporter when tied
    assert dave_pos_1 < reporter_pos_1, \
        "Dave and Reporter tied on points but not in consistent alphabetical order"
"
}
